blocks.text: The voltage of an electrochemical cell also depends on concentration, temperature and the pressure of any gas, so standard conditions are used when comparing electrode potentials: ions at 1.00 mol dm-3, a temperature of 25 degrees C (298 K), gases at 1 atmosphere (101 kPa), and the electrode potential of the half-cell measured relative to the standard hydrogen electrode. Under these conditions the electrode potential is the standard electrode potential, symbol E standard, spoken as 'E standard'.

blocks.title: Standard electrode potential
blocks.text: The standard electrode potential for a half-cell is the voltage measured under standard conditions with a standard hydrogen electrode as the other half-cell.

blocks.prompt: Why is a temperature and a concentration specified in the definition of E standard?
blocks.explanation: The electrode equilibrium, such as Cu2+ + 2e- = Cu, shifts with the ion concentration and with temperature, so the voltage changes with them. Fixing 1.00 mol dm-3, 298 K and 101 kPa makes the values of different half-cells comparable and lets them be tabulated.

items: Standard conditions: 1.00 mol dm-3, 298 K, 101 kPa, measured against the SHE; the voltage so measured is E standard.
